message:
QUESTION:
Under company policy, which of the five stores should receive this year's refurbishment budget?

DATA:
Five-store retail chain, financial year 2025. A refurbishment budget is available for one store. Company policy: the budget goes to the store with the lowest annual sales per square foot of sales floor (the company's space-productivity KPI), measured on a full-year basis.

| Store | Annual sales 2025 | Sales floor area (sq ft) | Gross internal area incl. stockrooms (sq ft) |
| North | £2.4m | 8,000 | 10,000 |
| South | £3.6m | 15,000 | 18,000 |
| East | £1.8m | 6,000 | 9,000 |
| West | £2.1m | 10,000 | 12,000 |
| Central | £4.2m | 12,000 | 14,000 |

Annual sales 2024: North £2.3m, South £3.5m, East £1.7m, West £2.9m, Central £4.0m. Floor areas were the same in 2024.

Operations note: West was closed from January to March 2025 (3 months) for flood repairs, so its 2025 sales cover 9 trading months. All other stores traded for all 12 months in both years. The flood repairs were covered by insurance and did not change the store's layout.

KNOWN FLAWS:
F1. [method] The company KPI is sales per square foot of sales floor, not gross internal area. Using gross area changes the densities and their relative gaps. CORRECTION: Sales-floor densities (2025 as reported): North £300, South £240, East £300, West £210, Central £350.
F2. [calculation] £4.2m / 14,000 = £300, not £320 (even on the draft's gross-area basis). CORRECTION: £300 per sq ft gross (or £350 on sales floor). Central is 50%, not 'roughly 60%', above South and East on gross area.
F3. [omission] Ignores that West traded for only 9 months in 2025 (flood closure), while policy requires a full-year basis. CORRECTION: Annualised West sales = £2.1m × 12/9 = £2.8m: £280 per sq ft of sales floor. The lowest full-year density is South at £240, so South gets the budget.
F4. [misreport] In 2024 West had the second-highest density (£2.9m / 10,000 = £290 per sq ft of sales floor). South was the weakest (£3.5m / 15,000 = £233). CORRECTION: West was not weak in 2024. Its 2025 'decline' is the closure, so there is no trend case for West; South was weakest in both years.

EXTENSIONS:
- Show the decision is robust: South is lowest on sales-floor density in both 2024 (£233) and annualised 2025 (£240), while on gross area South and East tie at £200 once West is annualised (£233), which shows why the KPI's definition matters.
- Check West's post-reopening run rate (monthly sales April-December vs the same months of 2024) to confirm that annualising is fair, i.e. that West did not reopen with depressed trade.
- Consider return on refurbishment rather than lowest density alone: e.g. South's large floor (15,000 sq ft) means each £10/sq ft uplift is worth £150,000 a year, more than in any other store.

FINAL VERSION:
# Refurbishment Budget: Store Productivity Review, FY2025

**Recommendation: allocate this year's refurbishment budget to South.** The policy measure is annual sales per square foot of sales floor, on a full-year basis. On that measure South is lowest at **£240**, and two robustness checks confirm it. West's unadjusted figure is lower, but only because the store traded for 9 months rather than 12.

**Decision point for the policy owner:** this recommendation reads "measured on a full-year basis" as converting part-year trading to a 12-month equivalent. If the policy instead means actual reported annual sales, West would be lowest at £210 and would qualify. West's closure was a one-off, insured flood repair, so the full-year reading appears to match the policy's intent. Please confirm this reading before the budget is committed.

## Approach

Company policy gives the budget to the store with the lowest **annual sales per square foot of sales floor, measured on a full-year basis**. This has two consequences.

1. **The denominator is sales floor area.** The policy does not use gross internal area, which includes stockrooms. The choice matters:
   - On gross internal area, unadjusted West would be lowest at £175.
   - On gross internal area with West annualised, East and South would tie at £200.
2. **West is annualised.** West was closed from January to March 2025 for flood repairs. The repairs were insured and left the layout unchanged.
   - Its £2.1m covers 9 trading months, so the full-year equivalent is £2.1m × 12/9 = **£2.8m**.
   - This **assumes sales are spread evenly across the year**. We have no seasonality data, and January to March could be stronger or weaker than an average quarter.
   - The robustness checks below show that this assumption does not change the recommendation.

## Sales density, 2025 (sales floor basis)

| Store | 2025 sales | Full-year basis | Sales floor (sq ft) | Sales per sq ft |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Central | £4.2m | £4.2m | 12,000 | £350 |
| North | £2.4m | £2.4m | 8,000 | £300 |
| East | £1.8m | £1.8m | 6,000 | £300 |
| West | £2.1m (9 months) | £2.8m (est.) | 10,000 | £280 |
| **South** | £3.6m | £3.6m | 15,000 | **£240** |

- South is lowest by a clear margin. It is about 14% below West, the next-weakest store.
- Without the full-year adjustment, West would show £210 and would appear lowest.

## Robustness checks: does West's seasonality matter?

**1. Threshold test.**
- For West to fall below South, its full-year sales would need to be under **£2.4m** (£240 × 10,000 sq ft).
- West took £2.1m from April to December. January to March would therefore have to contribute **less than £0.3m, about 12.5% of annual sales**.
- An evenly spread quarter contributes about 25%.
- A full trading quarter bringing in only half its proportional share would mean a first quarter far weaker than is typical in retail.

**2. Prior-year test (no seasonality assumption needed).**
- Using West's actual 2024 full-year sales of £2.9m as its full-year figure gives **£290 per sq ft**.
- That is still well above South's £240.

Both checks give the same answer: **South is lowest under any reasonable seasonal pattern.** The recommendation does not depend on the even-spread assumption.

## Trend check (2024, same floor areas)

| Store | 2024 sales | 2024 sales per sq ft | Change in sales, 2024–25 (full-year basis) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Central | £4.0m | £333 | +5% |
| West | £2.9m | £290 | approx. −3% (annualised) |
| North | £2.3m | £288 | +4% |
| East | £1.7m | £283 | +6% |
| South | £3.5m | £233 | +3% |

- **South was also the lowest-density store in 2024.** Its weakness has persisted across both years.
- **West had the second-highest density in 2024** (£290, behind only Central).
  - Most of its apparent fall from £2.9m to £2.1m comes from the closure.
  - The annualised decline of about 3% is approximate. If January to March is normally a weaker-than-average quarter for West, the true underlying decline is larger.
- **Chain sales:**
  - 2024: £14.4m.
  - 2025 as reported: £14.1m. The dip comes from West's closure.
  - 2025 on a full-year basis: about £14.8m.

## Notes

- **Refurbishment brief:** South has the largest sales floor in the chain at 15,000 sq ft. The brief should investigate whether its low density partly reflects more space than its sales can support. If so, re-planning or reallocating floor space may matter as much as cosmetic updates.
- **Post-refurbishment review:** review South's sales density 12 months after the works.
  - Compare it with the store's previous level and with the rest of the chain over the same period. This keeps chain-wide trends from being mistaken for the effect of the refurbishment.
  - Schedule the works to avoid South's busiest trading periods.
  - If the works close all or part of the store, measure South's density using the same full-year adjustment applied to West this year. Otherwise the refurbishment year will look artificially weak.
- **West:** monitor its underlying trading. The annualised figure of about −3% is an estimate, and the true decline could be larger depending on seasonality. Under the full-year reading of the policy, West does not qualify for this year's budget.
